decisions.reason: Define ADLBH.AVISIT enumerates the analysis labels without a period; the reference and derived evidence contain a nonblank period string, which is outside that codelist.

Original Define ADLBH.PARAM (line 4610) has Length=100; the _MCHC decode in PARAMCD_ADLBH is the concatenated label truncated to that storage length. Read with that constraint, the final missing letter is not a contradictory parameter rule.

Define ADLBH.PARAM concatenates the source test name and unit, while its codelist and the reference omit the HCT unit; the probe reads LB.LBTEST/LBSTRESU and its length reading separately checks the _MCHC decode. The reported Hematocrit label differences remain under that reading.

Original Define ValueList.ADLBH.A1HI links ordinary copy branches to LB.LBSTNRHI and relative-change branches to Set to missing (ItemDefs at lines 10298-10582). The reported comparison applies the ordinary copy to the relative-change records; ordinary reference A1HI values match the linked LB upper limits.

Define ADLBH.R2A1LO names A1HI despite its lower-limit label; SAP page-12 defines the ratios using their respective LLN and ULN. The full source context supplies no exception that reconciles those denominators.

The R2A1LO probe divides published AVAL by published A1HI and applies the precision stated in Define ADLBH.R2A1LO. Its SAP-limit reading changes the denominator as cited, but the evidence still shows differences including unrounded reference values.

Define ADLBH.R2A1HI names A1LO despite its upper-limit label; SAP page-12 defines the ratios using their respective LLN and ULN. The full source context supplies no exception that reconciles those denominators.

The R2A1HI probe divides published AVAL by published A1LO and applies the precision stated in Define ADLBH.R2A1HI. Its SAP-limit reading changes the denominator as cited, but the evidence still shows differences including unrounded reference values.

Define ADLBH.BR2A1LO names A1HI despite its lower-limit label; SAP page-12 defines the ratios using their respective LLN and ULN. The full source context supplies no exception that reconciles those denominators.

The BR2A1LO probe selects the published ABLFL baseline AVAL and A1HI, then applies Define ADLBH.BR2A1LO precision. SAP page-17 supports the baseline visit and page-12 supports the alternate denominator; neither reading reproduces the reference as reported.

Define ADLBH.BR2A1HI names A1LO despite its upper-limit label; SAP page-12 defines the ratios using their respective LLN and ULN. The full source context supplies no exception that reconciles those denominators.

The BR2A1HI probe selects the published ABLFL baseline AVAL and A1LO, then applies Define ADLBH.BR2A1HI precision. SAP page-17 supports the baseline visit and page-12 supports the alternate denominator; neither reading reproduces the reference as reported.

Define ADLBH.ALBTRVAL states the maximum of the two signed threshold excesses and its precision; the probe uses LB standard normal limits and the published LBSTRESN copy. The evidence shows the resulting signed values differ from the published positive threshold distances.
Define ADLBH.LBNRIND enumerates LOW, NORMAL and HIGH, with no value-level override. ABNORMAL in the reported reference and derived records is outside that list, even though it is transported from LB.

Define ADLBH.STUDYID names ADSL.STUDYID, but adlbh.yaml base-ord reads LB.STUDYID, using ONLY for grouped records. The ADSL_SBJ lookup is not used for this field, so the documented source has been replaced.

Define ADLBH.STUDYID names ADSL.STUDYID, but adlbh.yaml base-eot reads LB.STUDYID, using ONLY for grouped records. The ADSL_SBJ lookup is not used for this field, so the documented source has been replaced.

Define ADLBH.STUDYID names ADSL.STUDYID, but adlbh.yaml under-ord reads LB.STUDYID, using ONLY for grouped records. The ADSL_SBJ lookup is not used for this field, so the documented source has been replaced.

Define ADLBH.USUBJID names ADSL.USUBJID, while adlbh.yaml base-ord reads LB.USUBJID. The subject identifier is a key for the ADSL lookup but its output value is taken from LB.

SAP page-11 explicitly includes laboratory assessments in actual-date visit assignment. adlbh.yaml base-ord and under-ord instead map LB.VISIT labels and do not use assessment dates to assign AVISIT.
SAP page-11 defines visit-window days from randomization; the complete adlbh.yaml visit helpers and row branches do not calculate those days. ADY uses TRTSDT and is not used to assign AVISIT.
SAP page-11 requires the assessment closest to a window target when multiple assessments qualify. The adlbh.yaml rows and PREV helper contain no distance-to-target selection for AVISIT.
SAP page-11 includes retrieval assessments when selecting Week 24. Both ordinary adlbh.yaml row filters exclude RETRIEVAL before any selection, and the end-of-treatment filters also exclude it.
SAP page-11 resolves equal target distances by choosing the preceding assessment. No adlbh.yaml AVISIT branch or helper implements that comparison or tie rule.
Define ADLBH.ADY states LB.LBDY. adlbh.yaml ADY recalculates study day from _ADT_DATE and TRTSDT and never reads that source field, so matching values do not establish a copy path.

adlbh.yaml base-ord and under-ord copy LB.VISIT; base-eot and under-eot use ONLY(LB.VISIT) while grouping by the retained LBSEQ source key. These executable row derivations preserve the source named by Define ADLBH.VISIT.

adlbh.yaml base-ord and under-ord copy LB.VISITNUM; base-eot and under-eot use ONLY(LB.VISITNUM) while grouping by the retained LBSEQ source key. These executable row derivations preserve the source named by Define ADLBH.VISITNUM.

Define ADLBH.PARAM specifies LBTEST/LBSTRESU concatenation for ordinary parameters. Every adlbh.yaml row family instead obtains _PARAM_BASE from a fixed LBTESTCD dictionary, which omits the HCT unit and does not read the documented descriptor fields.

adlbh.yaml base-ord copies LB.LBSTNRHI and base-eot takes ONLY of that field; under-ord and under-eot set A1HI missing. Original Define ValueList.ADLBH.A1HI and its ordinary/underscore ItemDefs prescribe those same copy and missing branches.
Define ADLBH.R2A1LO divides by A1HI, while adlbh.yaml R2A1LO divides by A1LO. The baseline helpers for the BR variables do not remove this denominator difference.
Define ADLBH.R2A1HI divides by A1LO, while adlbh.yaml R2A1HI divides by A1HI. The baseline helpers for the BR variables do not remove this denominator difference.

Define ADLBH.BR2A1HI divides by A1LO, while adlbh.yaml BR2A1HI divides by A1HI. The baseline helpers for the BR variables do not remove this denominator difference.

Define ADLBH.ALBTRVAL uses result minus the upper threshold and lower threshold minus result. adlbh.yaml base-ord reverses both differences before taking their maximum; its source helpers do not reverse them back.

Define ADLBH.ALBTRVAL uses result minus the upper threshold and lower threshold minus result. adlbh.yaml base-eot reverses both differences before taking their maximum; its source helpers do not reverse them back.

SAP page-17 specifies Week -2/Visit 1 and original Define ADLBH.ABLFL.ANISO through .POLYCHR likewise require VISITNUM=1. adlbh.yaml base-ord tests LBBLFL instead; SDTM Define LB.LBBLFL names SCREENING without establishing that exact Visit 1 condition.

Define ADLBH.AENTMTFL explicitly requires Visit 12 or early discontinuation followed by the last analyte assessment. adlbh.yaml AENTMTFL flags derived end-of-treatment rows and the highest eligible LBSEQ without a Visit 12 or discontinuation condition.

SAP page-12 requires the last on-treatment observation; adlbh.yaml base-ord defines last by descending LBSEQ without chronological selection. SDTM Define LB.LBSEQ only describes a record identifier and does not establish that its ordering is observation time.

SAP page-12 requires the last on-treatment observation; adlbh.yaml base-eot defines last by descending LBSEQ without chronological selection. SDTM Define LB.LBSEQ only describes a record identifier and does not establish that its ordering is observation time.

adlbh.yaml base-ord and under-ord copy LB.LBNRIND, and both end-of-treatment row families use ONLY(LB.LBNRIND) with the retained LBSEQ key. The entire row logic therefore reads the source named in Define ADLBH.LBNRIND, despite the empty column-level derivation.

adlbh.yaml base-ord and under-ord copy LB.LBSTRESN, and both end-of-treatment row families use ONLY(LB.LBSTRESN) with the retained LBSEQ key. The entire row logic therefore reads the source named in Define ADLBH.LBSTRESN, despite the empty column-level derivation.

SAP pages 12 and 34 describe the last observed on-treatment value, but neither states that LBSEQ orders observation time. SDTM Define LB.LBSEQ describes an identifier only, so adlbh.yaml base-eot adds an unstated ordering source.
Define ADLBH.AVISIT and SAP pages 11-12 do not assign a period character to other collected visits. adlbh.yaml base-ord explicitly emits a nonblank period string for that case.

Original SAP page-11 includes laboratory actual-date assignment but its window table supplies bounds only for ADAS-Cog/CIBIC+ and NPI-X. Define ADLBH.AVISIT supplies labels without laboratory date bounds, leaving a complete date-window probe unspecified.

Original Define ValueList.ADLBH.AVAL links ordinary LB.LBSTRESN copies and underscore change/normal-range formulas, including baseline nulling and parameter-specific precision (ItemDefs at lines 11834-12152). SAP page-12 identifies the previous scheduled visit, so omission of those linked ItemDefs from the section adapter does not make the retained AVAL rule incomplete.

Original Define ADLBH.BASE ordinary ItemDefs (lines 12160-12308) select LBSTRESN when ADLBC.ABLFL=Y; ADLBC is the chemistry dataset and its parameter codes do not identify the hematology rows. The cross-dataset matching needed to apply that flag is unstated, although the underscore missing branches are documented.

Original Define ValueList.ADLBH.CHG links ordinary ItemDefs specifying AVAL - BASE and underscore ItemDefs specifying missing (lines 12758-13042), with parameter-specific precision. Those retained rules resolve subtraction order and applicability even though the adapter omits them.

Original Define ValueList.ADLBH.A1LO links ordinary LB.LBSTNRLO copies and underscore Set to missing branches (ItemDefs at lines 10590-10874), with parameter-specific numeric types and precision. This retained source and applicability are sufficient to state the rule; the adapter coverage limit is not documentary incompleteness.

Original Define ADLBH.ANL01FL ordinary and underscore ItemDefs (lines 11188-11518) specify ALBTRVAL versus absolute AVAL, Visits 4-12, and first-occurrence tie selection. Those variable-specific rules are present in the retained XML even though they are absent from the adapter sections.

adlbh.yaml base-ord adds _AVAL_BASE as a maximum candidate when A1LO is missing. Define ADLBH.ALBTRVAL and SAP page-12 state threshold differences without that raw-result fallback, and no retained section supplies it.

adlbh.yaml base-eot adds _AVAL_BASE as a maximum candidate when A1LO is missing. Define ADLBH.ALBTRVAL and SAP page-12 state threshold differences without that raw-result fallback, and no retained section supplies it.

Original Define ADLBH.ANRIND ordinary ItemDefs (lines 11528-11688) use LAVAL for the high comparison, but neither the retained ADLBH/LB definitions nor the datasets contain LAVAL. The underscore rules are documented, but the unresolved ordinary source prevents a complete literal rule.

Original Define ADLBH.BNRIND ordinary ItemDefs (lines 12452-12612) select ADLBH.ANRIND when ADLBH.ABLFL=Y and the underscore ItemDefs explicitly set missing. The retained XML therefore supplies the source and parameter applicability that the adapter omits.

Original Define ADLBH.ABLFL ordinary ItemDefs (lines 10882-11042) specify Y if VISITNUM=1, null otherwise, and the underscore ItemDefs set missing. Together with SAP page-17, this is a complete baseline flag rule; the absent adapter sections do not remove it.

Define ADLBH.AENTMTFL requires early discontinuation before Visit 12, but neither its section nor SAP pages 10, 12 and 17 specifies an operational discontinuation-to-visit comparison or washout duration. The available ADSL flags and dates do not state the missing linkage needed for the full treatment-phase selection.
